title: Writing and asking
description: Say what you write, what you send, and what you ask for.
grammarNote: An -ir verb in the present: escribo, escribes, escribe, escribimos, escribís, escriben.

explanation.summary: The -ir verbs are the third family, and they are the easiest of the three: the endings are the -er endings with an extra i in the tú and nosotros forms.

sections.heading: The six endings
sections.body: Drop the -ir and add -o, -es, -e, -imos, -ís, -en. Escribir becomes escribo, escribes, escribe, escribimos, escribís, escriben. Compare with the -er form: comes, comemos, coméis. The -ir form adds an i: escribes, escribimos, escribís.

examples.es: Abrimos la tienda a las diez.
examples.en: We open the shop at ten.

sections.heading: The yo form that changes
sections.body: A few -ir verbs change in the yo form only. Pedir becomes pido, which is irregular: the e is dropped. Servir becomes sirvo, and the e is dropped too. Most others are regular: comparto, decido, descubro.

sections.heading: Which one to use
sections.body: The three families are close enough that you can often guess the wrong one, so learn the ending of the infinitive with the verb: hablar, comer, vivir. The -ir verbs are the ones used for writing, opening, sharing and repeating, which is why they feel a little more modern than the rest.

examples.en: I share the table with you.
